message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Chapi CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  build:

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Set up JDK 11
      uses: actions/setup-java@v5
      with:
        distribution: temurin
        java-version: '11'

    - name: Setup Gradle
      uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6

    - name: Cache Gradle dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.gradle/caches
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}

    - name: Execute Gradle build
      run: ./gradlew build

    - name: Execute Gradle Coverage
      run: ./gradlew check

    - name: Upload coverage reports to Codecov
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The workflow uses Gradle with a wrapper and runs on three operating systems. Adding an explicit cache step for Gradle dependencies (~/.gradle/caches) keyed by OS and Gradle configuration files reduces repeated dependency downloads. This is supported by experimental evidence showing ~20% elapsed time savings for a similar Gradle workflow (experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) and the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern which recommends caching dependency downloads when repeated fetching is measurable and cache inputs include lockfiles and environment.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
